36 A 100 cm potentiometer wire QT is connected in series with a 2.00 V cell. Another circuit,
consisting of a 2.00 V cell in series with resistors of resistance 4.00 Ω and 6.00 Ω, is set up
alongside the potentiometer. Connections PQ and RS are then made so that the potential
difference (p.d.) across the 4.00 Ω resistor is balanced against the p.d. across a length L of
potentiometer wire. Both cells have negligible internal resistance.

hints: Notice the lower circuit: find the current through the $4.00\,\Omega$ and $6.00\,\Omega$ series resistors driven by the $2.00\,\text{V}$ cell.
Use $V = IR$ for the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor to get the p.d. between P and R that must be balanced by the wire QS.
Connect that p.d. to the uniform wire QT: the $2.00\,\text{V}$ driver falls uniformly over $100\,\text{cm}$, so length $L$ satisfies $V_{PR} = (2.00/100)L$.
walkthrough: Find the current in the lower test circuit. Total resistance is $4.00 + 6.00 = 10.0\,\Omega$, so $I = V/R = 2.00/10.0 = 0.20\,\text{A}$.
Find the p.d. to be balanced across the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor between P and R: $V_{PR} = IR = 0.20 \times 4.00 = 0.80\,\text{V}$.
Find the potential gradient along the uniform potentiometer wire QT. The $2.00\,\text{V}$ driver is spread over $100\,\text{cm}$, so gradient $k = 2.00/100 = 0.020\,\text{V cm}^{-1}$.
At balance no current flows in the galvanometer branch, so p.d. across length $L$ from Q to S equals $V_{PR}$: $kL = 0.80\,\text{V}$.
Solve for $L$: $L = 0.80/0.020 = 40\,\text{cm}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Zero length would mean zero p.d. across QS, but the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor carries current so its p.d. is not zero.

B.explanation: A p.d. of $0.80\,\text{V}$ across the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor balances a $40\,\text{cm}$ length at $0.020\,\text{V cm}^{-1}$ on the wire.

C.explanation: This length gives $1.20\,\text{V}$, which is the p.d. across the $6.00\,\Omega$ resistor, not the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor.

D.explanation: The full $100\,\text{cm}$ gives the full $2.00\,\text{V}$ driver p.d., which is larger than the $0.80\,\text{V}$ to be balanced.
